facts.raw_span: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms

concepts.why: Patient presents with worsening shortness of breath, New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and a prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation, all of which are indicative of acute decompensated heart failure.
Patient has a low blood pressure, elevated jugular venous pressure, and a prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation, which are all signs of cardiogenic shock.

Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, a single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, and a significantly decreased ejection fraction, all of which are indicative of ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Patient presents with worsening shortness of breath and bilateral lung crackles, which are indicative of pulmonary edema.
Patient has a heart rate of 106 beats per minute, which is indicative of atrial tachycardia.
Patient has elevated creatinine levels, which are indicative of renal insufficiency.
Patient presents with signs of substantial volume overload, including elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and a prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation.
Patient has a confirmed dual tachycardia, which is indicative of an abnormal heart rhythm.
Patient has an atypical left bundle-branch block morphology on their electrocardiogram, which is indicative of left bundle branch block.
Patient has variable PR intervals, which are indicative of atrioventricular dissociation.

rationales.F01: History of ischemic cardiomyopathy suggests a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F02: Ejection fraction of 25% indicates a moderate likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and a strong likelihood of Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F05: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms indicate a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Volume Overload.
rationales.F07: Heart rate of 106 beats/min suggests a moderate likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure, Cardiogenic Shock, Atrial Tachycardia, and Dual Tachycardia.
rationales.F09: Elevated jugular venous pressure indicates a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Volume Overload.
rationales.F10: Bilateral lung crackles on auscultation suggest a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Pulmonary Edema.
rationales.F11: Prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation indicates a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure and Volume Overload.
rationales.F12: Ejection fraction of 10% indicates a strong likelihood of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure, Ischemic Cardiomyopathy, and Cardiogenic Shock.
